given.why: Both loans are lent through the app and never returned, so they're open when the job runs.
The loans are due 2026-03-16 and the clock is set to 2026-03-17, so both are overdue and lines 29-35 expect both to be sent.
The clock is always set to 10:00Z, far from midnight, so code that works out 'today' from the local date instead of the UTC date would still pass in any normal CI timezone.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The database is fresh, so neither loan has a reminder before the job runs.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: The fake's `sent` must hold exactly two requests, each with the right memberId, loanId and dueOn, so a skipped call or the wrong member would fail.
The reminders table must hold exactly one row for each loan.
`sent_on` must be 2026-03-17, the clock's date, not the due date.

B3 proves this: if the job recorded before asking, the refused loan1 would get a row and B3's exact toEqual on the reminders table would fail. mutants.json leaves this part unmutated for the same reason.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on 2026-03-17, so on the second run loan1 already has a reminder for today.
loan2 is overdue but returned before the job runs.
The third loan is lent on 2026-03-03, so it's due 2026-03-17, the same day the job runs. That's the exact boundary.

then.why: toMatchObject on an array checks its length, so `sent` must be exactly one request, for loan1. A repeat for loan1 or any send for loan2 or loan3 would fail.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with a reason.
B5 proves that a failed connection reaches the job as a refusal, and the job only ever sees refusals, which this test covers.

then.why: An exact toEqual on the reminders table allows only loan2's row, so any row for loan1 would fail.
toContainEqual needs an exact log entry with this event name.
The expected entry's level is `warn`, and the match is exact.
The fields must be exactly loanId loan1, so the wrong id would fail.
`error` must equal the fake's refusal reason exactly.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: The refused loan1 is due earlier and was created first, and loan2 must still be sent and recorded afterwards, so stopping after the failure would fail.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans, one of them refused, all go through one run.

then.why: The last log entry must match exactly, with this event name.
The level must be `info`, and the match is exact.
`sent` must be 2.
`failed` must be 1.

given.why: Each test calls the real client's sendOverdueReminder with a reminder.

then.why: The recorded method must be POST, and the handler only matches POST. Other requests fail under onUnhandledRequest: "error".
The handler matches only `${NOTIFY_URL}/notifications`, and the recorded path must be `/notifications`.
The content-type must be application/json, and the body is read with request.json().
The body must have memberId set to member-1.

B5's assertion uses expect.objectContaining and never names `template`, so a renamed or missing template still passes B5. Only the borrow-a-book system test's B3 pins it (tests/system/borrow-a-book.system.test.ts:73), and that row doesn't promise this, so the check holds by luck.
`data` must equal exactly { loanId: loan-1, dueOn: 2026-03-16 }, so a renamed key would fail.
202, 200 and 204 must each come back as accepted, so code that accepts only 200 would fail.
Only a 400 is tried. A break that refuses only 4xx and accepts 5xx or 3xx would still pass.

then.part: or a failed connection as refused
then.why: HttpResponse.error() must come back as kind refused rather than throw.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain "400".

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The reason must contain "unreachable".
